SMTO-FIL-0053 — SMTO couldn't check which drives are connected

GUID: e8b2d606-177b-47e2-99aa-746f5c39422a
Slug: removable-inventory-unavailable
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • Before saving to a USB or external drive, SMTO asks the Gateway which drives are plugged in. That check failed, or the folder path given wasn't usable, so nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Execution target menu in the composer, select Refresh targets, and check that the Gateway for that computer shows as online. SMTO lists connected drives through the Gateway, so the Gateway must be reachable.
  2. Type the drive's full folder path in your message, for example "copy the report to /media/backup". When you name a folder yourself, SMTO checks that folder directly instead of listing every drive.
  3. If you typed a path, make sure it has no line breaks or pasted hidden characters and isn't extremely long. SMTO refuses folder paths with hidden control characters or more than 4,096 characters.
  4. If more than 32 drives are connected to that computer, unplug the ones you don't need. SMTO stops listing past 32 drives rather than guess which one you meant.

What success looks like

  • SMTO either asks you which drive to use or saves to the folder you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Removable destination protection just to make this go away; it stops files going to the wrong drive.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Removable-destination discovery failed (Gateway file operation unavailable, unsupported platform, incomplete inventory or more than 32 destinations), or an explicit destination path exceeded 4,096 characters or contained control characters.

What this means

  • Removable inventory cannot be obtained, the platform lacks the implementation, or an explicit destination path fails its bounded/control-character check. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Removable inventory cannot be obtained, the platform lacks the implementation, or an explicit destination path fails its bounded/control-character check.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish discovery failure from invalid explicit path syntax before changing Gateway configuration.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's removable_destinations file operation result and Gateway log (platform, psutil.disk_partitions, /sys/dev/block access). Restore Gateway connectivity and discovery, or have the user name a valid absolute destination path; keep removable_destination_guard_enabled on rather than disabling the check.
  • Restore the failing discovery prerequisite or correct the explicit destination path, then revalidate selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Current discovery or the supported explicit path validation establishes the intended destination.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.
